Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
11.6 SAFETY ANALYSES
SAF will be used for all safety analyses.
11.6.1 Adverse Events
All adverse events will be classified using the version of the MedDRA coding dictionary defined in the
Data Management Plan.
Events will be classified as treatment-emergent if they started or increased in severity on or after the
first date of Study Drug dosing and up to study closure or withdrawal date. If an event start date is
partial, then the start day, month, year or stop date will be used to determine if the event is treatment-
emergent. If the classification of the AE cannot be determined from the data available, then the event
will be considered treatment-emergent.
Adverse Reaction (AR) is defined as all untoward and unintended responses to an investigational
medicinal product (IMP) that are definitely related to any IMP dose administered. Serious Adverse
Reaction (SAR) is an AR which, in the eyes of the Investigator or the Sponsor:
• Results in death
• Is life-threatening adverse event (life-threatening means that the patient was at risk of death at
the time of the event and does not refer to a hypothetical situation where the event might have
caused death if it were more severe)
• Requires in-patient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalization
• Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity
• Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect
• Is a significant medical/surgical event, e.g. an event that jeopardises the patient or requires
intervention to prevent one of the above outcomes.
An overall summary of AEs will be produced (Table 14.3.1.1) including the number and % of patients
reporting at least 1 TEAE, the number and % of patients reporting at least 1 serious TEAE (where SAE
is reported as ‘Yes’), the number and % of patients reporting at least 1 AR, the number and % of patients
reporting at least 1 SAR, the number and % of patients reporting TEAEs by severity and relationship to
study treatment. A patient with multiple occurrences of any AE is counted only once at the maximum
level of severity or the strongest relationship to study treatment.
Adverse events will be described by primary system organ class and preferred term. Numbers and
percentage of patients, and number of occurrences of adverse event will be presented for:
• TEAE by SOC and PT (Table 14.3.1.2)
• TEAE by severity (Table 14.3.1.3)
• TEAE by relationship to VCN-01 (Table 14.3.1.4)
• TEAE by relationship to Gemcitabine (Table 14.3.1.5)
• TEAE by relationship to Nab-paclitaxel (Table 14.3.1.6)
• Serious TEAEs (Table 14.3.1.7)
• Drug-related TEAEs (where relationship is recorded as ‘Definitely Related’, ‘Probably Related’
or ‘Possibly Related’ for IMP or SoC) (Table 14.3.1.8)
• TEAEs leading to permanent discontinuation of study drug (where action is recorded as ‘Drug
Withdrawn’ for IMP or SoC) (Table 14.3.1.9)
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to VCN-01 (Table 14.3.1.10)
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to Gemcitabine (Table 14.3.1.11)

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to Nab-paclitaxel (Table 14.3.1.12)
All adverse events will be listed.
Adverse events due to disease progression will not be summarised, these adverse events will be listed
in a separate listing only.
If a patient has multiple AEs with the same preferred term, these will be summarised once within the
count for N (%) of patients, but each event will be counted within the number of reports n of each AE.
Changes in severity of the same AE (if collected) will be counted only once within the number of reports
n of each AE.
The following will be presented in listing format within the data summaries:
• Adverse Events leading to Deaths (Table 14.3.2.1)
• Serious Adverse Events (Table 14.3.2.2)
• Adverse Events which Led to Withdrawal (Table 14.3.2.3)
• Serious Adverse Reactions (Table 14.3.2.4)
11.6.2 Laboratory Data
Safety laboratory tests will be performed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in
the protocol (refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively). All laboratory
assessments are outlined in Section 9.2.1.
Laboratory data listings will be presented in two ways:
• Abnormal values (presented within the data summaries) (Table 14.3.3)
• All laboratory data (presented within the data listings)
The absolute values of each laboratory parameter (Biochemistry, Hematology, Coagulation, TSH,
Urinalysis) will be summarised at each visit along with the change from baseline to each post baseline
timepoint (Table 14.3.4.1 – Table 14.3.4.5). In addition, shift tables from baseline to each post baseline
timepoint will be presented (Table 14.3.4.6 – Table 14.3.4.10) to show Normal/ Abnormal Clinically
Significant (CS)/ Abnormal Not Clinically Significant (NCS) results.
If lab results are repeated at the same visit, the repeated result will be used in summaries (instead of the
original one) provided the sample was taken within the visit window, otherwise the original result will
be used. All results will be listed.
Lab results at unscheduled visits will be included in the listings but will not be summarised.
Serology and Pregnancy results will be listed only.
11.6.3 Vital Signs
Vital signs will be assessed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in the protocol
(refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
Vital signs will include supine systolic and diastolic blood pressure (mmHg), pulse (bpm), body
temperature (°C) and respiration rate. Body weight (kg) will also be recorded along with vital signs (pre-
dose only).

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
The absolute values of the vital signs including weight will be summarised at each visit along with the
change from baseline to each post baseline timepoint (Table 14.3.5.1). Height will be summarised within
the demography data. Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for
normal, abnormal NCS and abnormal CS vital signs results (Table 14.3.5.2).
11.6.4 Physical Examination
Full and abbreviated physical examinations will be performed at the time points provided in the schedule
of assessments in the protocol (refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for normal, abnormal NCS and
abnormal CS physical examination results by body system (Table 14.3.6).
11.6.5 Electrocardiogram
The absolute values of Heart rate, PR interval, RR interval, QRS width, QT interval and QTcF interval
will be summarised at each visit along with the change from baseline to each post baseline timepoint
(Table 14.3.7.1).
Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for normal, abnormal NCS and
abnormal CS ECG results (Table 14.3.7.2).
11.6.6 COVID-19 Testing
The patients will be required to undergo polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test to check for active
COVID-19 infection during the study.
COVID-19 testing results will be listed only.
11.6.7 Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF)
LVEF assessments will be performed at Screening and at other timepoints only if clinically indicated.
LVEF results will be listed only.
11.6.8 Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Score
ECOG score will be assessed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in the protocol
(refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
The ECOG Performance score is recorded at baseline (randomization) and at every visit thereafter. For
each level of the ECOG score, the proportion of patients continuing on that or a better score will be
estimated for each visit using Kaplan-Meier estimates. At death the patient will be assumed to have risen
to the highest ECOG score. This method of presentation will ignore those cases where a patient’s
ECOG score climbs and then falls again.
These proportions will be plotted for each treatment arm across time, a time to event figure will be
created. (Figure 14.3.1).
ECOG scores will be presented using number and percentage of patients by visit (Table 14.3.8).
11.6.9 Fibroscan
Fibroscan results will be listed only.

15 SHELLS FOR TABLES, FIGURES AND LISTINGS
The intended layouts for tables, figures and listings are presented. However, it may be appropriate for
the Simbec-Orion programmer to change the layouts, upon review of the data available, for
completeness and clarity.
QCd output will be produced as Rich Text Format (.rtf) or MS Word (.docx) files for convenient

to tables, listings and figures. Should this not be possible results will be provided in RTF of word
document format only.
Subject to this, the following will apply:
• Layout will be landscape, fixed width, font size 9, with margin size 2.54 cm for all sides.
• Each output will have the heading:

• Table headings will define the analysis set used for the summary/analysis.
• All outputs will have a footer specifying the SAS program path and filename (left); page x/y (right)

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
4.4 PHARMACOKINETIC VARIABLES
Pharmacokinetic variables are not evaluated in this study.
4.5 PHARMACODYNAMIC VARIABLES
Please refer to Section 4.3 for exploratory Pharmacodynamic variables. No further Pharmacodynamic
variables will be evaluated in this study.
4.6 SAFETY VARIABLES
Safety will be evaluated by the following:
• Demographics
• Medical history
• Prior medications and procedures, including standard of care
• Concomitant medications and procedures
• Physical examinations
• Vital signs assessments
• Safety laboratory test – biochemistry, hematology, coagulation profile, thyroid stimulating
hormone (TSH), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)/Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), tuberculosis (TB) test and
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), urinalysis and pregnancy test
• 12-Lead electrocardiogram (ECG)
• COVID-19 testing
• Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
• Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score
• Fibroscan (if clinically indicated)
• Adverse event (AE)/serious adverse event (SAE) assessment.
5 DEFINITIONS
Study Drug: Study drug is taken to mean either VCN-01 (considered as IMP) or nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine (considered as non-IMPs to be administrated as SoC).
Baseline: Baseline is defined by patient and by variable as the last non-missing value (including
repeat/unscheduled assessments) before the first dose of study drug except for QoL and ECOG result.
The baseline for QoL is C1D1, if not missing, otherwise the closes value which is before C1D1. The
baseline ECOG status refers to the ECOG assessment used to determine stratification at randomization.
This is always the Screening value. Study Day: Study day is the number of days since start of treatment
where the date of first dose is counted as Day 1 (there is no Day 0).
Protocol Deviation: a deviation related to study inclusion or exclusion criteria, conduct of the trial,
patient management or patient assessment. This refers to any change, divergence, or departure from
the study design or procedures defined in the protocol. Protocol deviations captured in the CRF will be
reviewed on a regular basis during the study and discussed at the Data Review Meeting (DRM) before
Database Lock (DBL). In addition, any deviations identified during the DRM will be discussed and included
in the database as necessary. All protocol deviations within the study database will be classified as either
‘Major’ or ‘Minor’ prior to DBL, details of which will be included within the Protocol Deviations Listing.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
6 ANALYSIS SETS
Membership of the analysis sets will be reviewed and agreed at a DRM before database lock.
6.1 ALL RANDOMIZED SET
The All Randomized Set is defined as all patients who are randomized.
This analysis set will be used for the summary of disposition.
6.2 SAFETY ANALYSIS SET (SAF)
The Safety Analysis Set (SAF) is defined as all patients who are randomized and take at least any dose of
Study Drug.
This analysis set will be used for demographic and safety summaries as well as for study listings. The
treatment arm is defined as the treatment that actually treated the patient.
6.3 INTENT-TO-TREAT SET (ITT)
The intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis set is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
any dose of Study Drug. The treatment arm is defined as the treatment that is randomized to treat the
patient.
The ITT will be used for demographic and baseline characteristics summary and for all efficacy analyses.
6.4 FULL ANALYSIS SET (FAS)
The Full Analysis Set (FAS) is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose, if allocated to Arm 1 or
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose and a complete dose of VCN-01, if allocated to
Arm II
during the first cycle of the study.
The FAS will be used for the efficacy analyses of the primary and secondary variables and for demographic
and baseline characteristics.
6.5 PER-PROTOCOL SET (PPS)
The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) is defined as patients in the FAS without any major protocol deviations that
could potentially influence a primary or main secondary study endpoint.
Primary analysis will be repeated for the PPS.
6.6 PHARMACODYNAMIC SET (PDS)
The Pharmacodynamic Set (PDS) will consist of all patients in the FAS who had at least 1
pharmacodynamic measurement, had no major protocol deviations affecting pharmacodynamic
parameters and no deviation from pharmacodynamic sampling procedures.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
Data will be summarised by treatment arm. Where appropriate, data will also be summarised by visit
with summaries for each visit attended as scheduled and an additional summary for final (last scheduled
visit or early withdrawal). The format of the summaries is defined in the shells at the end of this
document.
In summary and analysis tables of continuous variables, standard descriptive statistics (N, mean, standard
deviation [STD], median, minimum and maximum) will be presented. Least squares mean (LS mean),
standard error (SE) and 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented in the statistical analysis outputs
as appropriate. The minimum and maximum statistics will be presented in summary tables to the same
number of significant figures as the original data. The mean, median, LS mean, CI, STD and SE will be
presented to one more significant than the original data.
In summary tables of categorical variables, the number of non-missing observations by category will be
presented with percentages. Unless otherwise specified, the denominator for each percentage will be
the number of non-missing observations within the column. All percentages will be presented to one
decimal place.
If changes in severity for the same Treatment Emergent Adverse Event (TEAE) have been reported
separately but with the same AE number, they will be collapsed to a single AE with maximum severity
for the summary tables, but will be listed as reported.
Classifications of medical history, concomitant medication and adverse events will be sorted
alphabetically within the summary tables.
If any laboratory assessments are repeated at the same visit, the result from the repeat assessment will
be used in summaries. Both values will be listed.
Data collected on the eCRF will be presented within data listings. The data listings will be sorted by
treatment arm, patient number and visit. If any patients receive the wrong treatment this will be flagged
in all listings. For patients who complete the study, the last visit will be described in the listings as ‘<Cycle
X Day Y>’; for those who withdraw early it will be described as ‘End of Study’.
The date format for all output presentations will be ‘ddMMMyyyy’.
All statistical analysis will be performed using SAS® Enterprise Guide 8.3 or higher.
All hypothesis testing will be carried out at the 5% (2-sided) significance level unless stated otherwise.
P-values will be rounded to four decimal places. P-values less than 0.0001 will be reported as <0.0001
in tables.
If any of the assumptions underlying the formal statistical methods proposed are violated during the
analysis of the final data, alternative statistical methods will be used and any changes documented in the
statistical methods section of the CSR, including the rationale for use.
10.2 STRATIFICATION AND COVARIATE ADJUSTMENT
Randomization is stratified by ECOG (=0 or =1) at baseline and region (=NA or =EU). The primary
analysis will be adjusted for the stratification factors.
10.3 INTERACTIONS
No interactions are to be performed.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
11.6 SAFETY ANALYSES
SAF will be used for all safety analyses.
11.6.1 Adverse Events
All adverse events will be classified using the version of the MedDRA coding dictionary defined in the
Data Management Plan.
Events will be classified as treatment-emergent if they started or increased in severity on or after the
first date of Study Drug dosing and up to study closure or withdrawal date. If an event start date is
partial, then the start day, month, year or stop date will be used to determine if the event is treatment-
emergent. If the classification of the AE cannot be determined from the data available, then the event
will be considered treatment-emergent.
Adverse Reaction (AR) is defined as all untoward and unintended responses to an investigational
medicinal product (IMP) that are definitely related to any IMP dose administered. Serious Adverse
Reaction (SAR) is an AR which, in the eyes of the Investigator or the Sponsor:
• Results in death
• Is life-threatening adverse event (life-threatening means that the patient was at risk of death at
the time of the event and does not refer to a hypothetical situation where the event might have
caused death if it were more severe)
• Requires in-patient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalization
• Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity
• Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect
• Is a significant medical/surgical event, e.g. an event that jeopardises the patient or requires
intervention to prevent one of the above outcomes.
An overall summary of AEs will be produced (Table 14.3.1.1) including the number and % of patients
reporting at least 1 TEAE, the number and % of patients reporting at least 1 serious TEAE (where SAE
is reported as ‘Yes’), the number and % of patients reporting at least 1 AR, the number and % of patients
reporting at least 1 SAR, the number and % of patients reporting TEAEs by severity and relationship to
study treatment. A patient with multiple occurrences of any AE is counted only once at the maximum
level of severity or the strongest relationship to study treatment.
Adverse events will be described by primary system organ class and preferred term. Numbers and
percentage of patients, and number of occurrences of adverse event will be presented for:
• TEAE by SOC and PT (Table 14.3.1.2)
• TEAE by severity (Table 14.3.1.3)
• TEAE by relationship to VCN-01 (Table 14.3.1.4)
• TEAE by relationship to Gemcitabine (Table 14.3.1.5)
• TEAE by relationship to Nab-paclitaxel (Table 14.3.1.6)
• Serious TEAEs (Table 14.3.1.7)
• Drug-related TEAEs (where relationship is recorded as ‘Definitely Related’, ‘Probably Related’
or ‘Possibly Related’ for IMP or SoC) (Table 14.3.1.8)
• TEAEs leading to permanent discontinuation of study drug (where action is recorded as ‘Drug
Withdrawn’ for IMP or SoC) (Table 14.3.1.9)
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to VCN-01 (Table 14.3.1.10)
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to Gemcitabine (Table 14.3.1.11)

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to Nab-paclitaxel (Table 14.3.1.12)
All adverse events will be listed.
Adverse events due to disease progression will not be summarised, these adverse events will be listed
in a separate listing only.
If a patient has multiple AEs with the same preferred term, these will be summarised once within the
count for N (%) of patients, but each event will be counted within the number of reports n of each AE.
Changes in severity of the same AE (if collected) will be counted only once within the number of reports
n of each AE.
The following will be presented in listing format within the data summaries:
• Adverse Events leading to Deaths (Table 14.3.2.1)
• Serious Adverse Events (Table 14.3.2.2)
• Adverse Events which Led to Withdrawal (Table 14.3.2.3)
• Serious Adverse Reactions (Table 14.3.2.4)
11.6.2 Laboratory Data
Safety laboratory tests will be performed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in
the protocol (refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively). All laboratory
assessments are outlined in Section 9.2.1.
Laboratory data listings will be presented in two ways:
• Abnormal values (presented within the data summaries) (Table 14.3.3)
• All laboratory data (presented within the data listings)
The absolute values of each laboratory parameter (Biochemistry, Hematology, Coagulation, TSH,
Urinalysis) will be summarised at each visit along with the change from baseline to each post baseline
timepoint (Table 14.3.4.1 – Table 14.3.4.5). In addition, shift tables from baseline to each post baseline
timepoint will be presented (Table 14.3.4.6 – Table 14.3.4.10) to show Normal/ Abnormal Clinically
Significant (CS)/ Abnormal Not Clinically Significant (NCS) results.
If lab results are repeated at the same visit, the repeated result will be used in summaries (instead of the
original one) provided the sample was taken within the visit window, otherwise the original result will
be used. All results will be listed.
Lab results at unscheduled visits will be included in the listings but will not be summarised.
Serology and Pregnancy results will be listed only.
11.6.3 Vital Signs
Vital signs will be assessed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in the protocol
(refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
Vital signs will include supine systolic and diastolic blood pressure (mmHg), pulse (bpm), body
temperature (°C) and respiration rate. Body weight (kg) will also be recorded along with vital signs (pre-
dose only).

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
The absolute values of the vital signs including weight will be summarised at each visit along with the
change from baseline to each post baseline timepoint (Table 14.3.5.1). Height will be summarised within
the demography data. Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for
normal, abnormal NCS and abnormal CS vital signs results (Table 14.3.5.2).
11.6.4 Physical Examination
Full and abbreviated physical examinations will be performed at the time points provided in the schedule
of assessments in the protocol (refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for normal, abnormal NCS and
abnormal CS physical examination results by body system (Table 14.3.6).
11.6.5 Electrocardiogram
The absolute values of Heart rate, PR interval, RR interval, QRS width, QT interval and QTcF interval
will be summarised at each visit along with the change from baseline to each post baseline timepoint
(Table 14.3.7.1).
Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for normal, abnormal NCS and
abnormal CS ECG results (Table 14.3.7.2).
11.6.6 COVID-19 Testing
The patients will be required to undergo polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test to check for active
COVID-19 infection during the study.
COVID-19 testing results will be listed only.
11.6.7 Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF)
LVEF assessments will be performed at Screening and at other timepoints only if clinically indicated.
LVEF results will be listed only.
11.6.8 Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Score
ECOG score will be assessed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in the protocol
(refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
The ECOG Performance score is recorded at baseline (randomization) and at every visit thereafter. For
each level of the ECOG score, the proportion of patients continuing on that or a better score will be
estimated for each visit using Kaplan-Meier estimates. At death the patient will be assumed to have risen
to the highest ECOG score. This method of presentation will ignore those cases where a patient’s
ECOG score climbs and then falls again.
These proportions will be plotted for each treatment arm across time, a time to event figure will be
created. (Figure 14.3.1).
ECOG scores will be presented using number and percentage of patients by visit (Table 14.3.8).
11.6.9 Fibroscan
Fibroscan results will be listed only.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
15 SHELLS FOR TABLES, FIGURES AND LISTINGS
The intended layouts for tables, figures and listings are presented. However, it may be appropriate for
the Simbec-Orion programmer to change the layouts, upon review of the data available, for
completeness and clarity.
QCd output will be produced as Rich Text Format (.rtf) or MS Word (.docx) files for convenient
inclusion in the CSR. All attempts will be made to combine outputs into 3 pdf format files corresponding
to tables, listings and figures. Should this not be possible results will be provided in RTF of word
document format only.
Subject to this, the following will apply:
• Layout will be landscape, fixed width, font size 9, with margin size 2.54 cm for all sides.
• Each output will have the heading:
P-VCNA-003 (left); date and time ddMMMyyyy HH:MM(right)
• Table headings will define the analysis set used for the summary/analysis.
• All outputs will have a footer specifying the SAS program path and filename (left); page x/y (right)
• Tables will have a footer specifying the source listing
• Figures will have a footer specifying the source table or listing
• Additional footnotes will be included where appropriate for clarification.
• Treatment arm and patient number and will be included in all listings.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
4.4 PHARMACOKINETIC VARIABLES
Pharmacokinetic variables are not evaluated in this study.
4.5 PHARMACODYNAMIC VARIABLES
Please refer to Section 4.3 for exploratory Pharmacodynamic variables. No further Pharmacodynamic
variables will be evaluated in this study.
4.6 SAFETY VARIABLES
Safety will be evaluated by the following:
• Demographics
• Medical history
• Prior medications and procedures, including standard of care
• Concomitant medications and procedures
• Physical examinations
• Vital signs assessments
• Safety laboratory test – biochemistry, hematology, coagulation profile, thyroid stimulating
hormone (TSH), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)/Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), tuberculosis (TB) test and
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), urinalysis and pregnancy test
• 12-Lead electrocardiogram (ECG)
• COVID-19 testing
• Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
• Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score
• Fibroscan (if clinically indicated)
• Adverse event (AE)/serious adverse event (SAE) assessment.
5 DEFINITIONS
Study Drug: Study drug is taken to mean either VCN-01 (considered as IMP) or nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine (considered as non-IMPs to be administrated as SoC).
Baseline: Baseline is defined by patient and by variable as the last non-missing value (including
repeat/unscheduled assessments) before the first dose of study drug except for QoL and ECOG result.
The baseline for QoL is C1D1, if not missing, otherwise the closes value which is before C1D1. The
baseline ECOG status refers to the ECOG assessment used to determine stratification at randomization.
This is always the Screening value. Study Day: Study day is the number of days since start of treatment
where the date of first dose is counted as Day 1 (there is no Day 0).
Protocol Deviation: a deviation related to study inclusion or exclusion criteria, conduct of the trial,
patient management or patient assessment. This refers to any change, divergence, or departure from
the study design or procedures defined in the protocol. Protocol deviations captured in the CRF will be
reviewed on a regular basis during the study and discussed at the Data Review Meeting (DRM) before
Database Lock (DBL). In addition, any deviations identified during the DRM will be discussed and included
in the database as necessary. All protocol deviations within the study database will be classified as either
‘Major’ or ‘Minor’ prior to DBL, details of which will be included within the Protocol Deviations Listing.
Form STATt004

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
6 ANALYSIS SETS
Membership of the analysis sets will be reviewed and agreed at a DRM before database lock.
6.1 ALL RANDOMIZED SET
The All Randomized Set is defined as all patients who are randomized.
This analysis set will be used for the summary of disposition.
6.2 SAFETY ANALYSIS SET (SAF)
The Safety Analysis Set (SAF) is defined as all patients who are randomized and take at least any dose of
Study Drug.
This analysis set will be used for demographic and safety summaries as well as for study listings. The
treatment arm is defined as the treatment that actually treated the patient.
6.3 INTENT-TO-TREAT SET (ITT)
The intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis set is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
any dose of Study Drug. The treatment arm is defined as the treatment that is randomized to treat the
patient.
The ITT will be used for demographic and baseline characteristics summary and for all efficacy analyses.
6.4 FULL ANALYSIS SET (FAS)
The Full Analysis Set (FAS) is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose, if allocated to Arm 1 or
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose and a complete dose of VCN-01, if allocated to
Arm II
during the first cycle of the study.
The FAS will be used for the efficacy analyses of the primary and secondary variables and for demographic
and baseline characteristics.
6.5 PER-PROTOCOL SET (PPS)
The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) is defined as patients in the FAS without any major protocol deviations that
could potentially influence a primary or main secondary study endpoint.
Primary analysis will be repeated for the PPS.
6.6 PHARMACODYNAMIC SET (PDS)
The Pharmacodynamic Set (PDS) will consist of all patients in the FAS who had at least 1
pharmacodynamic measurement, had no major protocol deviations affecting pharmacodynamic
parameters and no deviation from pharmacodynamic sampling procedures.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
Data will be summarised by treatment arm. Where appropriate, data will also be summarised by visit
with summaries for each visit attended as scheduled and an additional summary for final (last scheduled
visit or early withdrawal). The format of the summaries is defined in the shells at the end of this
document.
In summary and analysis tables of continuous variables, standard descriptive statistics (N, mean, standard
deviation [STD], median, minimum and maximum) will be presented. Least squares mean (LS mean),
standard error (SE) and 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented in the statistical analysis outputs
as appropriate. The minimum and maximum statistics will be presented in summary tables to the same
number of significant figures as the original data. The mean, median, LS mean, CI, STD and SE will be
presented to one more significant than the original data.
In summary tables of categorical variables, the number of non-missing observations by category will be
presented with percentages. Unless otherwise specified, the denominator for each percentage will be
the number of non-missing observations within the column. All percentages will be presented to one
decimal place.
If changes in severity for the same Treatment Emergent Adverse Event (TEAE) have been reported
separately but with the same AE number, they will be collapsed to a single AE with maximum severity
for the summary tables, but will be listed as reported.
Classifications of medical history, concomitant medication and adverse events will be sorted
alphabetically within the summary tables.
If any laboratory assessments are repeated at the same visit, the result from the repeat assessment will
be used in summaries. Both values will be listed.
Data collected on the eCRF will be presented within data listings. The data listings will be sorted by
treatment arm, patient number and visit. If any patients receive the wrong treatment this will be flagged
in all listings. For patients who complete the study, the last visit will be described in the listings as ‘<Cycle
X Day Y>’; for those who withdraw early it will be described as ‘End of Study’.
The date format for all output presentations will be ‘ddMMMyyyy’.
All statistical analysis will be performed using SAS® Enterprise Guide 8.3 or higher.
All hypothesis testing will be carried out at the 5% (2-sided) significance level unless stated otherwise.
P-values will be rounded to four decimal places. P-values less than 0.0001 will be reported as <0.0001
in tables.
If any of the assumptions underlying the formal statistical methods proposed are violated during the
analysis of the final data, alternative statistical methods will be used and any changes documented in the
statistical methods section of the CSR, including the rationale for use.
10.2 STRATIFICATION AND COVARIATE ADJUSTMENT
Randomization is stratified by ECOG (=0 or =1) at baseline and region (=NA or =EU). The primary
analysis will be adjusted for the stratification factors.
10.3 INTERACTIONS
No interactions are to be performed.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
11.6 SAFETY ANALYSES
SAF will be used for all safety analyses.
11.6.1 Adverse Events
All adverse events will be classified using the version of the MedDRA coding dictionary defined in the
Data Management Plan.
Events will be classified as treatment-emergent if they started or increased in severity on or after the
first date of Study Drug dosing and up to study closure or withdrawal date. If an event start date is
partial, then the start day, month, year or stop date will be used to determine if the event is treatment-
emergent. If the classification of the AE cannot be determined from the data available, then the event
will be considered treatment-emergent.
Adverse Reaction (AR) is defined as all untoward and unintended responses to an investigational
medicinal product (IMP) that are definitely related to any IMP dose administered. Serious Adverse
Reaction (SAR) is an AR which, in the eyes of the Investigator or the Sponsor:
• Results in death
• Is life-threatening adverse event (life-threatening means that the patient was at risk of death at
the time of the event and does not refer to a hypothetical situation where the event might have
caused death if it were more severe)
• Requires in-patient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalization
• Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity
• Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect
• Is a significant medical/surgical event, e.g. an event that jeopardises the patient or requires
intervention to prevent one of the above outcomes.
An overall summary of AEs will be produced (Table 14.3.1.1) including the number and % of patients
reporting at least 1 TEAE, the number and % of patients reporting at least 1 serious TEAE (where SAE
is reported as ‘Yes’), the number and % of patients reporting at least 1 AR, the number and % of patients
reporting at least 1 SAR, the number and % of patients reporting TEAEs by severity and relationship to
study treatment. A patient with multiple occurrences of any AE is counted only once at the maximum
level of severity or the strongest relationship to study treatment.
Adverse events will be described by primary system organ class and preferred term. Numbers and
percentage of patients, and number of occurrences of adverse event will be presented for:
• TEAE by SOC and PT (Table 14.3.1.2)
• TEAE by severity (Table 14.3.1.3)
• TEAE by relationship to VCN-01 (Table 14.3.1.4)
• TEAE by relationship to Gemcitabine (Table 14.3.1.5)
• TEAE by relationship to Nab-paclitaxel (Table 14.3.1.6)
• Serious TEAEs (Table 14.3.1.7)
• Drug-related TEAEs (where relationship is recorded as ‘Definitely Related’, ‘Probably Related’
or ‘Possibly Related’ for IMP or SoC) (Table 14.3.1.8)
• TEAEs leading to permanent discontinuation of study drug (where action is recorded as ‘Drug
Withdrawn’ for IMP or SoC) (Table 14.3.1.9)
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to VCN-01 (Table 14.3.1.10)
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to Gemcitabine (Table 14.3.1.11)

Statistical Analysis Plan
• Serious TEAE by SOC, PT and relationship to Nab-paclitaxel (Table 14.3.1.12)
All adverse events will be listed.
Adverse events due to disease progression will not be summarised, these adverse events will be listed
in a separate listing only.
If a patient has multiple AEs with the same preferred term, these will be summarised once within the
count for N (%) of patients, but each event will be counted within the number of reports n of each AE.
Changes in severity of the same AE (if collected) will be counted only once within the number of reports
n of each AE.
The following will be presented in listing format within the data summaries:
• Adverse Events leading to Deaths (Table 14.3.2.1)
• Serious Adverse Events (Table 14.3.2.2)
• Adverse Events which Led to Withdrawal (Table 14.3.2.3)
• Serious Adverse Reactions (Table 14.3.2.4)
11.6.2 Laboratory Data
Safety laboratory tests will be performed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in
the protocol (refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively). All laboratory
assessments are outlined in Section 9.2.1.
Laboratory data listings will be presented in two ways:
• Abnormal values (presented within the data summaries) (Table 14.3.3)
• All laboratory data (presented within the data listings)
The absolute values of each laboratory parameter (Biochemistry, Hematology, Coagulation, TSH,
Urinalysis) will be summarised at each visit along with the change from baseline to each post baseline
timepoint (Table 14.3.4.1 – Table 14.3.4.5). In addition, shift tables from baseline to each post baseline
timepoint will be presented (Table 14.3.4.6 – Table 14.3.4.10) to show Normal/ Abnormal Clinically
Significant (CS)/ Abnormal Not Clinically Significant (NCS) results.
If lab results are repeated at the same visit, the repeated result will be used in summaries (instead of the
original one) provided the sample was taken within the visit window, otherwise the original result will
be used. All results will be listed.
Lab results at unscheduled visits will be included in the listings but will not be summarised.
Serology and Pregnancy results will be listed only.
11.6.3 Vital Signs
Vital signs will be assessed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in the protocol
(refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
Vital signs will include supine systolic and diastolic blood pressure (mmHg), pulse (bpm), body
temperature (°C) and respiration rate. Body weight (kg) will also be recorded along with vital signs (pre-
dose only).

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
The absolute values of the vital signs including weight will be summarised at each visit along with the
change from baseline to each post baseline timepoint (Table 14.3.5.1). Height will be summarised within
the demography data. Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for
normal, abnormal NCS and abnormal CS vital signs results (Table 14.3.5.2).
11.6.4 Physical Examination
Full and abbreviated physical examinations will be performed at the time points provided in the schedule
of assessments in the protocol (refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for normal, abnormal NCS and
abnormal CS physical examination results by body system (Table 14.3.6).
11.6.5 Electrocardiogram
The absolute values of Heart rate, PR interval, RR interval, QRS width, QT interval and QTcF interval
will be summarised at each visit along with the change from baseline to each post baseline timepoint
(Table 14.3.7.1).
Shift tables will be presented showing changes from baseline to each visit for normal, abnormal NCS and
abnormal CS ECG results (Table 14.3.7.2).
11.6.6 COVID-19 Testing
The patients will be required to undergo polymerase chain reaction (PCR) test to check for active
COVID-19 infection during the study.
COVID-19 testing results will be listed only.
11.6.7 Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF)
LVEF assessments will be performed at Screening and at other timepoints only if clinically indicated.
LVEF results will be listed only.
11.6.8 Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Score
ECOG score will be assessed at the time points provided in the schedule of assessments in the protocol
(refer to APPENDIX 7 and APPENDIX 8 for Arms I and II, respectively).
The ECOG Performance score is recorded at baseline (randomization) and at every visit thereafter. For
each level of the ECOG score, the proportion of patients continuing on that or a better score will be
estimated for each visit using Kaplan-Meier estimates. At death the patient will be assumed to have risen
to the highest ECOG score. This method of presentation will ignore those cases where a patient’s
ECOG score climbs and then falls again.
These proportions will be plotted for each treatment arm across time, a time to event figure will be
created. (Figure 14.3.1).
ECOG scores will be presented using number and percentage of patients by visit (Table 14.3.8).
11.6.9 Fibroscan
Fibroscan results will be listed only.

15 SHELLS FOR TABLES, FIGURES AND LISTINGS
The intended layouts for tables, figures and listings are presented. However, it may be appropriate for
the Simbec-Orion programmer to change the layouts, upon review of the data available, for
completeness and clarity.
QCd output will be produced as Rich Text Format (.rtf) or MS Word (.docx) files for convenient
inclusion in the CSR. All attempts will be made to combine outputs into 3 pdf format files corresponding
to tables, listings and figures. Should this not be possible results will be provided in RTF of word
document format only.
Subject to this, the following will apply:
• Layout will be landscape, fixed width, font size 9, with margin size 2.54 cm for all sides.
• Each output will have the heading:
P-VCNA-003 (left); date and time ddMMMyyyy HH:MM(right)
• Table headings will define the analysis set used for the summary/analysis.
• All outputs will have a footer specifying the SAS program path and filename (left); page x/y (right)
• Tables will have a footer specifying the source listing
• Figures will have a footer specifying the source table or listing
• Additional footnotes will be included where appropriate for clarification.
• Treatment arm and patient number and will be included in all listings.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
4.4 PHARMACOKINETIC VARIABLES
Pharmacokinetic variables are not evaluated in this study.
4.5 PHARMACODYNAMIC VARIABLES
Please refer to Section 4.3 for exploratory Pharmacodynamic variables. No further Pharmacodynamic
variables will be evaluated in this study.
4.6 SAFETY VARIABLES
Safety will be evaluated by the following:
• Demographics
• Medical history
• Prior medications and procedures, including standard of care
• Concomitant medications and procedures
• Physical examinations
• Vital signs assessments
• Safety laboratory test – biochemistry, hematology, coagulation profile, thyroid stimulating
hormone (TSH), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)/Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), tuberculosis (TB) test and
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), urinalysis and pregnancy test
• 12-Lead electrocardiogram (ECG)
• COVID-19 testing
• Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
• Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score
• Fibroscan (if clinically indicated)
• Adverse event (AE)/serious adverse event (SAE) assessment.
5 DEFINITIONS
Study Drug: Study drug is taken to mean either VCN-01 (considered as IMP) or nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine (considered as non-IMPs to be administrated as SoC).
Baseline: Baseline is defined by patient and by variable as the last non-missing value (including
repeat/unscheduled assessments) before the first dose of study drug except for QoL and ECOG result.
The baseline for QoL is C1D1, if not missing, otherwise the closes value which is before C1D1. The
baseline ECOG status refers to the ECOG assessment used to determine stratification at randomization.
This is always the Screening value. Study Day: Study day is the number of days since start of treatment
where the date of first dose is counted as Day 1 (there is no Day 0).
Protocol Deviation: a deviation related to study inclusion or exclusion criteria, conduct of the trial,
patient management or patient assessment. This refers to any change, divergence, or departure from
the study design or procedures defined in the protocol. Protocol deviations captured in the CRF will be
reviewed on a regular basis during the study and discussed at the Data Review Meeting (DRM) before
Database Lock (DBL). In addition, any deviations identified during the DRM will be discussed and included
in the database as necessary. All protocol deviations within the study database will be classified as either
‘Major’ or ‘Minor’ prior to DBL, details of which will be included within the Protocol Deviations Listing.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
6 ANALYSIS SETS
Membership of the analysis sets will be reviewed and agreed at a DRM before database lock.
6.1 ALL RANDOMIZED SET
The All Randomized Set is defined as all patients who are randomized.
This analysis set will be used for the summary of disposition.
6.2 SAFETY ANALYSIS SET (SAF)
The Safety Analysis Set (SAF) is defined as all patients who are randomized and take at least any dose of
Study Drug.
This analysis set will be used for demographic and safety summaries as well as for study listings. The
treatment arm is defined as the treatment that actually treated the patient.
6.3 INTENT-TO-TREAT SET (ITT)
The intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis set is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
any dose of Study Drug. The treatment arm is defined as the treatment that is randomized to treat the
patient.
The ITT will be used for demographic and baseline characteristics summary and for all efficacy analyses.
6.4 FULL ANALYSIS SET (FAS)
The Full Analysis Set (FAS) is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose, if allocated to Arm 1 or
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose and a complete dose of VCN-01, if allocated to
Arm II
during the first cycle of the study.
The FAS will be used for the efficacy analyses of the primary and secondary variables and for demographic
and baseline characteristics.
6.5 PER-PROTOCOL SET (PPS)
The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) is defined as patients in the FAS without any major protocol deviations that
could potentially influence a primary or main secondary study endpoint.
Primary analysis will be repeated for the PPS.
6.6 PHARMACODYNAMIC SET (PDS)
The Pharmacodynamic Set (PDS) will consist of all patients in the FAS who had at least 1
pharmacodynamic measurement, had no major protocol deviations affecting pharmacodynamic
parameters and no deviation from pharmacodynamic sampling procedures.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
Data will be summarised by treatment arm. Where appropriate, data will also be summarised by visit
with summaries for each visit attended as scheduled and an additional summary for final (last scheduled
visit or early withdrawal). The format of the summaries is defined in the shells at the end of this
document.
In summary and analysis tables of continuous variables, standard descriptive statistics (N, mean, standard
deviation [STD], median, minimum and maximum) will be presented. Least squares mean (LS mean),
standard error (SE) and 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented in the statistical analysis outputs
as appropriate. The minimum and maximum statistics will be presented in summary tables to the same
number of significant figures as the original data. The mean, median, LS mean, CI, STD and SE will be
presented to one more significant than the original data.
In summary tables of categorical variables, the number of non-missing observations by category will be
presented with percentages. Unless otherwise specified, the denominator for each percentage will be
the number of non-missing observations within the column. All percentages will be presented to one
decimal place.
If changes in severity for the same Treatment Emergent Adverse Event (TEAE) have been reported
separately but with the same AE number, they will be collapsed to a single AE with maximum severity
for the summary tables, but will be listed as reported.
Classifications of medical history, concomitant medication and adverse events will be sorted
alphabetically within the summary tables.
If any laboratory assessments are repeated at the same visit, the result from the repeat assessment will
be used in summaries. Both values will be listed.
Data collected on the eCRF will be presented within data listings. The data listings will be sorted by
treatment arm, patient number and visit. If any patients receive the wrong treatment this will be flagged
in all listings. For patients who complete the study, the last visit will be described in the listings as ‘<Cycle
X Day Y>’; for those who withdraw early it will be described as ‘End of Study’.
The date format for all output presentations will be ‘ddMMMyyyy’.
All statistical analysis will be performed using SAS® Enterprise Guide 8.3 or higher.
All hypothesis testing will be carried out at the 5% (2-sided) significance level unless stated otherwise.
P-values will be rounded to four decimal places. P-values less than 0.0001 will be reported as <0.0001
in tables.
If any of the assumptions underlying the formal statistical methods proposed are violated during the
analysis of the final data, alternative statistical methods will be used and any changes documented in the
statistical methods section of the CSR, including the rationale for use.
10.2 STRATIFICATION AND COVARIATE ADJUSTMENT
Randomization is stratified by ECOG (=0 or =1) at baseline and region (=NA or =EU). The primary
analysis will be adjusted for the stratification factors.
10.3 INTERACTIONS
No interactions are to be performed.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
11.6.10 Anticancer treatment
Anticancer treatment after discontinuation in the trial will be summarized by treatment arms using
Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical 4 (ATC4) term and preferred term (Table 14.3.9).
11.7 STUDY DRUG EXPOSURE AND COMPLIANCE
Treatment duration (days), number of doses administered, total dose administered, dose intensity
(represents the amount of a drug administered per dosing day) and relative dose intensity (actual dose
intensity delivered to the standard planned dose intensity per dosing day) will be described by descriptive
statistics for each of the treatments (VCN-01, Nab-paclitaxel, Gemcitabine) by treatment arm.
Incidence of dose prolongation (yes, no), dose interruption (yes, no) and dose reduction (yes, no, reason
for reduction – applicable for Nab-paclitaxel and Gemcitabine only) will be presented descriptively using
number of events, number of patients and percentage.
Treatment compliance, as percentage of injection administered (actual/planned) will be summarized by
visit and overall.
Treatment exposure and compliance will be summarised for the FAS (Table 14.3.10).
11.8 PRIOR AND CONCOMITANT MEDICATIONS AND PROCEDURES
Prior medications/medical procedures are defined as any medication taken/any medical procedures
performed within 28 days of the Screening visit. Any medication taken at or after the time of the
Screening visit, regardless of whether it had started prior to the study or not, until EoS visit is to be
recorded as concomitant medication.
Therapies will be classified using the version of the World Health Organisation Drug Dictionary
(WHODD) coding dictionary defined in the Data Management Plan. The ATC Classification and WHO-
DRUG PT will be used to list and summarise the data.
The number (%) of patients reporting the use of any prior medications and the number (%) of patients
taking each drug by ATC classification and PT will be summarised using the SAF (Table 14.3.11.1). This
table will be repeated for concomitant medications (Table 14.3.11.2).
11.9 ALL OTHER DATA
All other data (Protocol Deviations, Inclusion/ Exclusion Criteria Failures, Obstetric History, Menopausal
Status, Drug Administration, Target and Non-Target Lesions) will be listed.
12 VALIDATION
All tables, figures and listings will be subject to independent quality control and visual review. Unique
tables will be independently programmed. Findings will be documented in a quality control form and
actions taken will also be documented.
The completed form will be reviewed and signed by both programmers and by the lead statistician.

Statistical Analysis Plan
15 SHELLS FOR TABLES, FIGURES AND LISTINGS
The intended layouts for tables, figures and listings are presented. However, it may be appropriate for
the Simbec-Orion programmer to change the layouts, upon review of the data available, for
completeness and clarity.
QCd output will be produced as Rich Text Format (.rtf) or MS Word (.docx) files for convenient
inclusion in the CSR. All attempts will be made to combine outputs into 3 pdf format files corresponding
to tables, listings and figures. Should this not be possible results will be provided in RTF of word
document format only.
Subject to this, the following will apply:
• Layout will be landscape, fixed width, font size 9, with margin size 2.54 cm for all sides.
• Each output will have the heading:
P-VCNA-003 (left); date and time ddMMMyyyy HH:MM(right)
• Table headings will define the analysis set used for the summary/analysis.
• All outputs will have a footer specifying the SAS program path and filename (left); page x/y (right)
• Tables will have a footer specifying the source listing
• Figures will have a footer specifying the source table or listing
• Additional footnotes will be included where appropriate for clarification.
• Treatment arm and patient number and will be included in all listings.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
4.4 PHARMACOKINETIC VARIABLES
Pharmacokinetic variables are not evaluated in this study.
4.5 PHARMACODYNAMIC VARIABLES
Please refer to Section 4.3 for exploratory Pharmacodynamic variables. No further Pharmacodynamic
variables will be evaluated in this study.
4.6 SAFETY VARIABLES
Safety will be evaluated by the following:
• Demographics
• Medical history
• Prior medications and procedures, including standard of care
• Concomitant medications and procedures
• Physical examinations
• Vital signs assessments
• Safety laboratory test – biochemistry, hematology, coagulation profile, thyroid stimulating
hormone (TSH), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)/Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), tuberculosis (TB) test and
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), urinalysis and pregnancy test
• 12-Lead electrocardiogram (ECG)
• COVID-19 testing
• Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
• Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score
• Fibroscan (if clinically indicated)
• Adverse event (AE)/serious adverse event (SAE) assessment.
5 DEFINITIONS
Study Drug: Study drug is taken to mean either VCN-01 (considered as IMP) or nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine (considered as non-IMPs to be administrated as SoC).
Baseline: Baseline is defined by patient and by variable as the last non-missing value (including
repeat/unscheduled assessments) before the first dose of study drug except for QoL and ECOG result.
The baseline for QoL is C1D1, if not missing, otherwise the closes value which is before C1D1. The
baseline ECOG status refers to the ECOG assessment used to determine stratification at randomization.
This is always the Screening value. Study Day: Study day is the number of days since start of treatment
where the date of first dose is counted as Day 1 (there is no Day 0).
Protocol Deviation: a deviation related to study inclusion or exclusion criteria, conduct of the trial,
patient management or patient assessment. This refers to any change, divergence, or departure from
the study design or procedures defined in the protocol. Protocol deviations captured in the CRF will be
reviewed on a regular basis during the study and discussed at the Data Review Meeting (DRM) before
Database Lock (DBL). In addition, any deviations identified during the DRM will be discussed and included
in the database as necessary. All protocol deviations within the study database will be classified as either
‘Major’ or ‘Minor’ prior to DBL, details of which will be included within the Protocol Deviations Listing.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
6 ANALYSIS SETS
Membership of the analysis sets will be reviewed and agreed at a DRM before database lock.
6.1 ALL RANDOMIZED SET
The All Randomized Set is defined as all patients who are randomized.
This analysis set will be used for the summary of disposition.
6.2 SAFETY ANALYSIS SET (SAF)
The Safety Analysis Set (SAF) is defined as all patients who are randomized and take at least any dose of
Study Drug.
This analysis set will be used for demographic and safety summaries as well as for study listings. The
treatment arm is defined as the treatment that actually treated the patient.
6.3 INTENT-TO-TREAT SET (ITT)
The intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis set is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
any dose of Study Drug. The treatment arm is defined as the treatment that is randomized to treat the
patient.
The ITT will be used for demographic and baseline characteristics summary and for all efficacy analyses.
6.4 FULL ANALYSIS SET (FAS)
The Full Analysis Set (FAS) is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose, if allocated to Arm 1 or
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose and a complete dose of VCN-01, if allocated to
Arm II
during the first cycle of the study.
The FAS will be used for the efficacy analyses of the primary and secondary variables and for demographic
and baseline characteristics.
6.5 PER-PROTOCOL SET (PPS)
The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) is defined as patients in the FAS without any major protocol deviations that
could potentially influence a primary or main secondary study endpoint.
Primary analysis will be repeated for the PPS.
6.6 PHARMACODYNAMIC SET (PDS)
The Pharmacodynamic Set (PDS) will consist of all patients in the FAS who had at least 1
pharmacodynamic measurement, had no major protocol deviations affecting pharmacodynamic
parameters and no deviation from pharmacodynamic sampling procedures.

evidence.exact_text:
Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
Data will be summarised by treatment arm. Where appropriate, data will also be summarised by visit
with summaries for each visit attended as scheduled and an additional summary for final (last scheduled
visit or early withdrawal). The format of the summaries is defined in the shells at the end of this
document.
In summary and analysis tables of continuous variables, standard descriptive statistics (N, mean, standard
deviation [STD], median, minimum and maximum) will be presented. Least squares mean (LS mean),
standard error (SE) and 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented in the statistical analysis outputs
as appropriate. The minimum and maximum statistics will be presented in summary tables to the same
number of significant figures as the original data. The mean, median, LS mean, CI, STD and SE will be
presented to one more significant than the original data.
In summary tables of categorical variables, the number of non-missing observations by category will be
presented with percentages. Unless otherwise specified, the denominator for each percentage will be
the number of non-missing observations within the column. All percentages will be presented to one
decimal place.
If changes in severity for the same Treatment Emergent Adverse Event (TEAE) have been reported
separately but with the same AE number, they will be collapsed to a single AE with maximum severity
for the summary tables, but will be listed as reported.
Classifications of medical history, concomitant medication and adverse events will be sorted
alphabetically within the summary tables.
If any laboratory assessments are repeated at the same visit, the result from the repeat assessment will
be used in summaries. Both values will be listed.
Data collected on the eCRF will be presented within data listings. The data listings will be sorted by
treatment arm, patient number and visit. If any patients receive the wrong treatment this will be flagged
in all listings. For patients who complete the study, the last visit will be described in the listings as ‘<Cycle
X Day Y>’; for those who withdraw early it will be described as ‘End of Study’.
The date format for all output presentations will be ‘ddMMMyyyy’.
All statistical analysis will be performed using SAS® Enterprise Guide 8.3 or higher.
All hypothesis testing will be carried out at the 5% (2-sided) significance level unless stated otherwise.
P-values will be rounded to four decimal places. P-values less than 0.0001 will be reported as <0.0001
in tables.
If any of the assumptions underlying the formal statistical methods proposed are violated during the
analysis of the final data, alternative statistical methods will be used and any changes documented in the
statistical methods section of the CSR, including the rationale for use.
10.2 STRATIFICATION AND COVARIATE ADJUSTMENT
Randomization is stratified by ECOG (=0 or =1) at baseline and region (=NA or =EU). The primary
analysis will be adjusted for the stratification factors.
10.3 INTERACTIONS
No interactions are to be performed.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
11.6.10 Anticancer treatment
Anticancer treatment after discontinuation in the trial will be summarized by treatment arms using
Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical 4 (ATC4) term and preferred term (Table 14.3.9).
11.7 STUDY DRUG EXPOSURE AND COMPLIANCE
Treatment duration (days), number of doses administered, total dose administered, dose intensity
(represents the amount of a drug administered per dosing day) and relative dose intensity (actual dose
intensity delivered to the standard planned dose intensity per dosing day) will be described by descriptive
statistics for each of the treatments (VCN-01, Nab-paclitaxel, Gemcitabine) by treatment arm.
Incidence of dose prolongation (yes, no), dose interruption (yes, no) and dose reduction (yes, no, reason
for reduction – applicable for Nab-paclitaxel and Gemcitabine only) will be presented descriptively using
number of events, number of patients and percentage.
Treatment compliance, as percentage of injection administered (actual/planned) will be summarized by
visit and overall.
Treatment exposure and compliance will be summarised for the FAS (Table 14.3.10).
11.8 PRIOR AND CONCOMITANT MEDICATIONS AND PROCEDURES
Prior medications/medical procedures are defined as any medication taken/any medical procedures
performed within 28 days of the Screening visit. Any medication taken at or after the time of the
Screening visit, regardless of whether it had started prior to the study or not, until EoS visit is to be
recorded as concomitant medication.
Therapies will be classified using the version of the World Health Organisation Drug Dictionary
(WHODD) coding dictionary defined in the Data Management Plan. The ATC Classification and WHO-
DRUG PT will be used to list and summarise the data.
The number (%) of patients reporting the use of any prior medications and the number (%) of patients
taking each drug by ATC classification and PT will be summarised using the SAF (Table 14.3.11.1). This
table will be repeated for concomitant medications (Table 14.3.11.2).
11.9 ALL OTHER DATA
All other data (Protocol Deviations, Inclusion/ Exclusion Criteria Failures, Obstetric History, Menopausal
Status, Drug Administration, Target and Non-Target Lesions) will be listed.
12 VALIDATION
All tables, figures and listings will be subject to independent quality control and visual review. Unique
tables will be independently programmed. Findings will be documented in a quality control form and
actions taken will also be documented.
The completed form will be reviewed and signed by both programmers and by the lead statistician.

15 SHELLS FOR TABLES, FIGURES AND LISTINGS
The intended layouts for tables, figures and listings are presented. However, it may be appropriate for
the Simbec-Orion programmer to change the layouts, upon review of the data available, for
completeness and clarity.
QCd output will be produced as Rich Text Format (.rtf) or MS Word (.docx) files for convenient
inclusion in the CSR. All attempts will be made to combine outputs into 3 pdf format files corresponding
to tables, listings and figures. Should this not be possible results will be provided in RTF of word
document format only.
Subject to this, the following will apply:
• Layout will be landscape, fixed width, font size 9, with margin size 2.54 cm for all sides.
• Each output will have the heading:
P-VCNA-003 (left); date and time ddMMMyyyy HH:MM(right)
• Table headings will define the analysis set used for the summary/analysis.
• All outputs will have a footer specifying the SAS program path and filename (left); page x/y (right)
• Tables will have a footer specifying the source listing
• Figures will have a footer specifying the source table or listing
• Additional footnotes will be included where appropriate for clarification.
• Treatment arm and patient number and will be included in all listings.

4.4 PHARMACOKINETIC VARIABLES
Pharmacokinetic variables are not evaluated in this study.
4.5 PHARMACODYNAMIC VARIABLES
Please refer to Section 4.3 for exploratory Pharmacodynamic variables. No further Pharmacodynamic
variables will be evaluated in this study.
4.6 SAFETY VARIABLES
Safety will be evaluated by the following:
• Demographics
• Medical history
• Prior medications and procedures, including standard of care
• Concomitant medications and procedures
• Physical examinations
• Vital signs assessments
• Safety laboratory test – biochemistry, hematology, coagulation profile, thyroid stimulating
hormone (TSH), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)/Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), tuberculosis (TB) test and
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), urinalysis and pregnancy test
• 12-Lead electrocardiogram (ECG)
• COVID-19 testing
• Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
• Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score
• Fibroscan (if clinically indicated)
• Adverse event (AE)/serious adverse event (SAE) assessment.
5 DEFINITIONS
Study Drug: Study drug is taken to mean either VCN-01 (considered as IMP) or nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine (considered as non-IMPs to be administrated as SoC).
Baseline: Baseline is defined by patient and by variable as the last non-missing value (including
repeat/unscheduled assessments) before the first dose of study drug except for QoL and ECOG result.
The baseline for QoL is C1D1, if not missing, otherwise the closes value which is before C1D1. The
baseline ECOG status refers to the ECOG assessment used to determine stratification at randomization.
This is always the Screening value. Study Day: Study day is the number of days since start of treatment
where the date of first dose is counted as Day 1 (there is no Day 0).
Protocol Deviation: a deviation related to study inclusion or exclusion criteria, conduct of the trial,
patient management or patient assessment. This refers to any change, divergence, or departure from
the study design or procedures defined in the protocol. Protocol deviations captured in the CRF will be
reviewed on a regular basis during the study and discussed at the Data Review Meeting (DRM) before
Database Lock (DBL). In addition, any deviations identified during the DRM will be discussed and included
in the database as necessary. All protocol deviations within the study database will be classified as either
‘Major’ or ‘Minor’ prior to DBL, details of which will be included within the Protocol Deviations Listing.

Statistical Analysis Plan
6 ANALYSIS SETS
Membership of the analysis sets will be reviewed and agreed at a DRM before database lock.
6.1 ALL RANDOMIZED SET
The All Randomized Set is defined as all patients who are randomized.
This analysis set will be used for the summary of disposition.
6.2 SAFETY ANALYSIS SET (SAF)
The Safety Analysis Set (SAF) is defined as all patients who are randomized and take at least any dose of
Study Drug.
This analysis set will be used for demographic and safety summaries as well as for study listings. The
treatment arm is defined as the treatment that actually treated the patient.
6.3 INTENT-TO-TREAT SET (ITT)
The intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis set is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
any dose of Study Drug. The treatment arm is defined as the treatment that is randomized to treat the
patient.
The ITT will be used for demographic and baseline characteristics summary and for all efficacy analyses.
6.4 FULL ANALYSIS SET (FAS)
The Full Analysis Set (FAS) is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose, if allocated to Arm 1 or
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose and a complete dose of VCN-01, if allocated to
Arm II
during the first cycle of the study.
The FAS will be used for the efficacy analyses of the primary and secondary variables and for demographic
and baseline characteristics.
6.5 PER-PROTOCOL SET (PPS)
The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) is defined as patients in the FAS without any major protocol deviations that
could potentially influence a primary or main secondary study endpoint.
Primary analysis will be repeated for the PPS.
6.6 PHARMACODYNAMIC SET (PDS)
The Pharmacodynamic Set (PDS) will consist of all patients in the FAS who had at least 1
pharmacodynamic measurement, had no major protocol deviations affecting pharmacodynamic
parameters and no deviation from pharmacodynamic sampling procedures.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
Data will be summarised by treatment arm. Where appropriate, data will also be summarised by visit
with summaries for each visit attended as scheduled and an additional summary for final (last scheduled
visit or early withdrawal). The format of the summaries is defined in the shells at the end of this
document.
In summary and analysis tables of continuous variables, standard descriptive statistics (N, mean, standard
deviation [STD], median, minimum and maximum) will be presented. Least squares mean (LS mean),
standard error (SE) and 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented in the statistical analysis outputs
as appropriate. The minimum and maximum statistics will be presented in summary tables to the same
number of significant figures as the original data. The mean, median, LS mean, CI, STD and SE will be
presented to one more significant than the original data.
In summary tables of categorical variables, the number of non-missing observations by category will be
presented with percentages. Unless otherwise specified, the denominator for each percentage will be
the number of non-missing observations within the column. All percentages will be presented to one
decimal place.
If changes in severity for the same Treatment Emergent Adverse Event (TEAE) have been reported
separately but with the same AE number, they will be collapsed to a single AE with maximum severity
for the summary tables, but will be listed as reported.
Classifications of medical history, concomitant medication and adverse events will be sorted
alphabetically within the summary tables.
If any laboratory assessments are repeated at the same visit, the result from the repeat assessment will
be used in summaries. Both values will be listed.
Data collected on the eCRF will be presented within data listings. The data listings will be sorted by
treatment arm, patient number and visit. If any patients receive the wrong treatment this will be flagged
in all listings. For patients who complete the study, the last visit will be described in the listings as ‘<Cycle
X Day Y>’; for those who withdraw early it will be described as ‘End of Study’.
The date format for all output presentations will be ‘ddMMMyyyy’.
All statistical analysis will be performed using SAS® Enterprise Guide 8.3 or higher.
All hypothesis testing will be carried out at the 5% (2-sided) significance level unless stated otherwise.
P-values will be rounded to four decimal places. P-values less than 0.0001 will be reported as <0.0001
in tables.
If any of the assumptions underlying the formal statistical methods proposed are violated during the
analysis of the final data, alternative statistical methods will be used and any changes documented in the
statistical methods section of the CSR, including the rationale for use.
10.2 STRATIFICATION AND COVARIATE ADJUSTMENT
Randomization is stratified by ECOG (=0 or =1) at baseline and region (=NA or =EU). The primary
analysis will be adjusted for the stratification factors.
10.3 INTERACTIONS
No interactions are to be performed.

Statistical Analysis Plan
Instructions can be found in the following figure.
11.3.3.2 Disease Control Rate (DCR) to the subsequent therapies
DCR for patients with subsequent anti-cancer therapies will be presented using the number and
percentage of patients (Table 14.2.3.2).
DCR will also be analysed using data from central imaging vendor (Table 14.2.3.3).
11.4 PHARMACOKINETIC ANALYSES
Not applicable.
11.5 PHARMACODYNAMIC ANALYSES
The following pharmacodynamic endpoints will be analysed: VCN-01 genomes in blood (Arm II only);
PH20 in serum (Arm II only); circulating immune markers in serum; neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio;
neutralizing anti-VCN-01 antibodies (Anti-Ad-NAbs) (Arm II only) in serum; image biomarkers
(radiomics) assessed from the images of CT scans performed during the study.
Pharmacodynamic parameters will be summarized using the Pharmacodynamic Set (Table 14.5.1). For
parameters applicable only for Arm II, paired t-test will be used to compare baseline and post baseline
values for continuous variables, and CMH or Chi-square test will be used for categorical variables. If
both Arms have values for a parameter, t-test will be used to compare change from baseline values at
each visit for continuous variables, and Chi-square test to compare the two Arms at each visit.
Depending on the findings, additional exploratory analyses may be conducted.

15 SHELLS FOR TABLES, FIGURES AND LISTINGS
The intended layouts for tables, figures and listings are presented. However, it may be appropriate for
the Simbec-Orion programmer to change the layouts, upon review of the data available, for
completeness and clarity.
QCd output will be produced as Rich Text Format (.rtf) or MS Word (.docx) files for convenient
inclusion in the CSR. All attempts will be made to combine outputs into 3 pdf format files corresponding
to tables, listings and figures. Should this not be possible results will be provided in RTF of word
document format only.
Subject to this, the following will apply:
• Layout will be landscape, fixed width, font size 9, with margin size 2.54 cm for all sides.
• Each output will have the heading:
P-VCNA-003 (left); date and time ddMMMyyyy HH:MM(right)
• Table headings will define the analysis set used for the summary/analysis.
• All outputs will have a footer specifying the SAS program path and filename (left); page x/y (right)
• Tables will have a footer specifying the source listing
• Figures will have a footer specifying the source table or listing
• Additional footnotes will be included where appropriate for clarification.

Theriva Biologics, S.L. P-VCNA-003
Statistical Analysis Plan
• End of Study (EOS): Patients will be followed for survival until the EOS regardless of further
treatments, or until the sponsor ends the study. Early trial termination of the study by the
Sponsor is only anticipated on the basis of safety.
See Protocol Appendix 7 and 8 for the Study Schedule in Arm I and Arm II.
3.5 SAMPLE SIZE CONSIDERATIONS
Assuming an accrual time of 18 months with (minimum) 12-month FU for all patients, 1-sided
alpha = 0.05, beta= 0.2 (80% power), the median OS=10.6 months for Arm I and the median OS=20.8
for Arm II with 1: 1 randomization, 46 patients would be needed for each study arm to reach the 57
events needed using the logrank test. It is therefore planned to randomize a total of 92 adult patients
with metastatic pancreatic cancer into the study for final analysis.
3.6 RANDOMIZATION
Patients will be randomized in a ratio of 1:1 to receive either SoC or SoC + 2 administrations of VCN-
01. The randomization will be stratified to take account of the patients’ baseline ECOG performance
status (0 or 1) and region (NA or EU).
4 STUDY VARIABLES AND COVARIATES
4.1 PRIMARY VARIABLES
The primary variables are:
• Overall Survival (OS)
• Safety and tolerability of VCN-01 in Arm II
4.2 SECONDARY VARIABLES
The secondary variables are:
• PFS or TTP
• ORR
• DCR (SD + PR + CR)
• Landmark 1-year survival and PFS at the 1-year landmark
• DoR
• Changes in tumor marker Ca 19.9
4.3 EXPLORATORY VARIABLES
The exploratory variables are:
• Biomarker levels, such as PH20, VCN-01 genomes, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio, anti-Ad-NAb,
circulating immune markers and/or other markers according to the state of the art, may be
determined in blood and serum samples collected at different timepoints during the study.
• Image biomarkers (radiomics) assessed from the images of CT scans performed during the study.
• Change from baseline in values of the QoL via the validated EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire
(version 3).
• DCR (SD + PR + CR) to the subsequent therapies.
